Use trusted caret metadata, never user pi:c text or a second wrapping algorithm. Define supported actual dimensions before removing preview clamps; no silent default parity outside the domain.

exactParityBoundaries.logical: Text/expanded text/UTF16 scalar cursor/paste/history/undo/callback/receipt structures remain source-exact. No sanitization rewrites editor storage.
exactParityBoundaries.component: Actual default shared source component rows, borders, source scrolling and fake-caret ANSI/APC are byte-exact to unchanged Editor.render expectations; raw rows are an oracle, not a transport-trust boundary.
exactParityBoundaries.transport: For benign text, preserve visible glyph/cell/style/caret semantics using source terminal normalizations. Native VT command framing/diff strategy may differ and raw source/native writes are both retained. Unsafe user-control output cannot be source-wire-identical while preventing terminal effects; every such conflict requires the explicit decision and retained differences below.

safeTransportDecision.state: PENDING explicit lead profile decision; recommended single safe default, no unsafe toggle or new optional profile
minimumRequirements: User-origin bytes never gain terminal control authority, including byte-identical SGR and forged cursor markers
Use only validated map cursor/focus/style metadata; do not infer caret by searching component strings
HT/LF are handled as declared normalized text/row boundaries; C0/C1/ESC and recognized CSI/OSC/APC/DCS/string payloads require an explicit data-display rule
An invisible drop must preserve proved source cell-prefix positions; visible escaping requires the SAME shared map for navigation/wrapping/caret. Neither may silently change source geometry

Untrusted packet/caret seams are non-additive: a caret inside a CSI/OSC can break the source packet, expose payload glyphs, and change emitted width. A blanket row-string strip is not enough. Retain these exact witnesses and reject unsupported unsafe conversion atomically until its rule is defined

Record deliberate control/forged-marker source-wire deviations as explicit profile exceptions pending qualification; do not normalize expected source objects or close original P5-08/09 from safe plain Unicode alone

concreteConflicts.conflict: Source passes clipboard-write OSC52 from SetText and InsertText; safe transport must suppress that authority.
Source passes ESC[999;999H from draft data; safe transport must prevent cursor movement.

Input a+pi:c+bc makes source extract the first user marker and position hardware at row2/column2 rather than the genuine end-of-abc column4; the genuine marker remains in the terminal output. Typed provenance fixes it by deliberately differing from unsafe source behavior.
A scalar seam inside a user ANSI packet changes source visible payload/style parsing; safe output needs a declared shared width/mapping rule, not post-render replacement.
Raw recalled NEL/CR reach source wire but can change physical rows despite source zero-cell accounting. Default safe transport cannot emit them merely to match raw source bytes.

encoderRules.authority: Factory-only style/cursor metadata derived from a construction-validated map. A syntactic VT allowlist does not make byte-identical user SGR/APC trusted.
encoderRules.data: The selected user-control rule must produce Unicode text with no raw C0/C1/ESC. Preserve surrogate validity and source zero-width/spacing semantics; emit user text only as data, never append an ANSI-bearing source row.
encoderRules.commandGrammar: Only fixed encoder-owned SGR0/7, bounded CUP, ED2J, EL2K and cursor visibility/mode commands; any protocol normalization such as OSC8 close is a fixed encoder action rather than a URL/data command. All dynamic numeric operands are validated against current frame dimensions.
encoderRules.tests: Parse the joined writes with a strict host-command grammar and compare expected trusted command counts/style spans/caret anchors. Assert no OSC52, title change, URL-open OSC8, DCS, arbitrary APC, unbounded CUP or C1 command. Keep parser state across write boundaries. Test byte-identical user SGR7 and pi:c in addition to existing adversarial witnesses.
encoderRules.rowBudget: Bound text, style-span count, row count, cells and encoded command overhead before transport admission; no prefix of an invalid frame is written. Keep immutable frames and existing actual-write completion/cache discipline.

additionalRequiredDecisions.evidence: columns1 and2 with CJK source Editor.render throws recursive RangeError; native source builder rejects ResourceLimit. Choose a bounded supported terminal fallback; no recursion/crash emulation.

Current preview clamps geometry256cols/64rows; source map/projector acceptsheight1024 and can emit309 rows, exceeding default TerminalFrame row256/text65536 limits. Choose a declared domain and coherent map/frame/write budgets, preserving outside-domain failures.

Source false hardware-cursor option hides the cursor but positions its focused marker for IME; focus loss retains inverse fake caret while no marker/anchor exists. Native current always-visible cursor is a different behavior to reconcile explicitly.

Captured layout has no scroll-reset/focus/startup signal. Current initial view draw precedes the authoritative controller. Approve the minimum new metadata/initial capture contract before implementation.
